registrations.packaging: Type II Hydrolytic Resistance Glass Bottle x 250 mL and 500 mL

summary: Nephrosteril (Fresenius Kabi) is a 7% amino acid solution for infusion without carbohydrates or electrolytes, intended for patients with renal insufficiency: 60% essential, 13% conditionally essential and 27% non-essential amino acids. Philippine registration: 250 ml and 500 ml glass bottles.
composition_notes: The manufacturer describes it as a 7% amino acid solution without carbohydrates and electrolytes (Fresenius Kabi India product page).
Lysine is given as L-lysine monoacetate and cysteine as acetylcysteine; the equivalent free amino acid amounts are shown in the rows marked "=".
dosing_limits: Acute and chronic renal insufficiency without dialysis: up to 0.5 g amino acids/kg body weight per day (500 ml per day at 70 kg).

Acute and chronic renal insufficiency on hemodialysis, hemofiltration or peritoneal dialysis: up to 1 g amino acids/kg body weight per day (1000 ml per day at 70 kg) (Fresenius Kabi India product page).
kidney_notes: Uses stated by the manufacturer: total or partial parenteral nutrition in acute or chronic renal insufficiency, with or without kidney replacement therapy, and intradialytic amino acid supplementation in maintenance hemodialysis.
It supplies amino acids only (no glucose, lipid or electrolytes): energy, electrolytes, vitamins and trace elements must be given separately and monitored.
guideline_heading: How it fits the ESPEN 2021 kidney nutrition guideline
guideline: ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 24: "No disease-specific enteral nor parenteral formula oriented for patients with reduced kidney function should be routinely utilized in every patient with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF in comparison to conventional formulas. Instead, their use is to be individualized (see recommendation 26)." Grade of recommendation B – Consensus (87.5% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 26: "In selected patients with electrolyte and fluid imbalances, concentrated “renal” EN or PN formulas with lower electrolyte content may be preferred over standard formulas." Grade of recommendation GPP – Strong consensus (95.7% agreement). (GPP, good practice point.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 18 (Grade of recommendation 0 – Consensus (82.6% agreement)): protein intakes that may be prescribed are 0.6–0.8 g/kg body weight (BW)/d for a hospitalized patient with CKD without acute/critical illness; 1.2 g/kg BW/d with CKD and KF on conventional intermittent chronic KRT without acute/critical illness; 0.8–1.0 g/kg BW/d with AKI or AKI on CKD without acute/critical illness; start with 1 g/kg BW/day and gradually increase up to 1.3 g/kg BW/d if tolerated with acute/critical illness not on KRT; 1.3–1.5 g/kg/d for critically ill patients on conventional intermittent KRT; and 1.5 g/kg/d up to 1.7 g/kg/d for critically ill patients on continuous KRT (CKRT) or prolonged intermittent KRT (PIKRT). "If available, the pre-hospitalization body weight or usual body weight may be preferred over the ideal BW. Actual BW should not be considered for a protein prescription." (AKI, acute kidney injury.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 25: "The choice of the most appropriate EN or PN formula should be made based on the calorie and protein ratio to provide the most accurate dosing in clinical practice." Grade of recommendation B – Strong consensus (91.3% agreement). (PN, parenteral nutrition.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 31: "Electrolytes abnormalities are common in patients with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF receiving KRT and shall be closely monitored." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (100% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 4: "Intradialytic parenteral nutrition (IDPN) shall be applied in malnourished non-critically ill hospitalized patients with CKD and KF on hemodialysis, or the same patients if at risk of malnutrition that fail to respond or do not tolerate ONS or EN." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (91.7% agreement). (CKD, chronic kidney disease; KF, kidney failure; ONS, oral nutritional supplements; EN, enteral nutrition.)
bottom_line: A renal amino acid formula (70 g amino acids per liter, no carbohydrates or electrolytes). ESPEN 2021 does not support routine use of kidney-specific PN formulas over conventional ones (Recommendation 24); concentrated renal formulas may be preferred in selected patients with electrolyte and fluid imbalances (Recommendation 26). Count it in the protein prescription and add energy and electrolytes separately.
